```{r setup}
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

here::i_am("README.qmd")

# kableExtra styling is LaTeX-only; the GitHub README build takes plain pipe tables.
latex_out <- knitr::is_latex_output()

# kableExtra's styling verbs emit LaTeX and have no meaning under gfm, where the same
# table renders as a pipe table. Each call site says what LaTeX alone gets.
latex_only <- function(k, f) if (latex_out) f(k) else k

gt <- read_csv(here::here("ground_truth", "schwarz_coppock_2022_ground_truth.csv"),
               col_types = cols(.default = col_character(), match = col_integer(),
                                match_rewrite = col_integer()))
claims <- read_csv(here::here("ground_truth", "published_claims_reproduction.csv"),
                   col_types = cols(.default = col_character(),
                                    match_rewrite = col_integer()))
manifest <- read_csv(here::here("original_manifest.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

# The errata's entries are data: errata.qmd defines them once and writes them here. Every
# count of them in this report reads that file rather than being typed, so the note and the
# report cannot state different numbers of corrections.
spine <- read_csv(here::here("errata_entries.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
n_errata <- nrow(spine)

# The prose spells small counts out, so a count read from a file has to be spelled too.
spelled <- function(n) {
  words <- c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine", "ten")
  if (n <= length(words)) words[n] else as.character(n)
}

# The significance-count paragraph and the Figure A.18 paragraph below restate errata entries
# 2 and 3. Both read the pipeline outputs the errata reads, so neither can carry a number the
# errata has since recomputed.
sig_counts <- read_csv(here::here("maintained", "output", "text_in_text_numbers.csv"),
                       show_col_types = FALSE)
study_level <- read_csv(here::here("maintained", "output", "text_study_level.csv"),
                        show_col_types = FALSE)
plotted_cells <- read_csv(here::here("maintained", "output",
                                     "figure_a2_a45_plotted_estimates.csv"),
                          show_col_types = FALSE)
n_costa <- sum(plotted_cells$figure_number == 18)

# Any significance rule is a threshold on the ratio of an estimate to its standard error.
# Tightening it until 23 positive estimates survive, and loosening it until 11 negative ones
# do, brackets what any such rule can reach.
sig_z <- abs(study_level$estimate / study_level$std.error)
negatives_at_23 <- sum(study_level$estimate < 0 &
                         sig_z >= sort(sig_z[study_level$estimate > 0], decreasing = TRUE)[23])
positives_at_11 <- sum(study_level$estimate > 0 &
                         sig_z >= sort(sig_z[study_level$estimate < 0], decreasing = TRUE)[11])
```

*Drafted by Claude Opus 5 under the supervision of Alex Coppock.*

This repository holds the actively maintained replication code for Schwarz and Coppock (2022), together with the reproducibility report that documents what the original archive did and did not do. It is part of a program applying the maintenance proposal in Peer, Orr and Coppock (2021, *PS: Political Science & Politics*, doi [10.1017/S1049096521000366](https://doi.org/10.1017/S1049096521000366)) to a set of published archives.

| | |
|---|---|
| Article | [10.1086/716290](https://doi.org/10.1086/716290) |
| Replication archive | [10.7910/DVN/R27ULT](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/R27ULT) |

**The data are not redistributed here.** The deposit is `r round(sum(manifest$bytes) / 1024^2, 1)` MB across `r nrow(manifest)` files and lives at Harvard Dataverse, which is the only copy this repository points at. `download_original.R` fetches it and verifies every file; `original_manifest.csv` pins the file identifiers, sizes and checksums, so the exact bytes this code was written against are recorded in version control even though the bytes themselves are not.

**Repository layout.** `maintained/` is the maintained rewrite: one script per published table or figure, writing to `output/`, which is committed so a reader can compare a fresh run against it without downloading anything. `ground_truth/` ties every published number to the code that produces it. `original/` is created by the download script and is deliberately absent from the repository. This file is the reproducibility report, also available as a PDF in `report/`.

**License.** CC0 1.0 Universal, matching the terms of the deposit this repository maintains. See `LICENSE`.

**To reproduce.** Clone or download the repository, open `schwarz_coppock_2022.Rproj`, and run:

``` r
source("run_all.R")
```

That fetches the deposit, verifies its `r nrow(manifest)` files, and produces every table and figure into `maintained/output/`. Required packages: tidyverse, metafor, knitr, kableExtra, here. Paths resolve through `here`, so nothing depends on the working directory. The full run takes about six seconds. A successful run overwrites `maintained/output/`, which is committed: **`git diff` on that folder is the reproduction check.**

# Summary

```{r summary_setup, include=FALSE}
n_claims <- nrow(gt)
n_verifiable <- sum(!is.na(gt$match))
n_match <- sum(gt$match == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
n_fail <- sum(gt$match == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
n_unverifiable <- sum(is.na(gt$match))
n_rewrite_match <- sum(gt$match_rewrite == 1, na.rm = TRUE)

n_published <- nrow(claims)
n_published_reproduced <- sum(claims$match_rewrite == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
n_published_disagree <- sum(claims$match_rewrite == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
n_published_no_counterpart <- sum(is.na(claims$match_rewrite))
is_plotted_label <- str_detect(claims$claim_id, " :: (estimate|std_error)$")
n_figure_cells <- sum(claims$location %in% c("figure_1", "figure_2", "figure_3", "figure_4") &
                        is_plotted_label)
n_appendix_cells <- sum(str_detect(claims$location, "^figure_a\\d+$") & is_plotted_label)
n_table_1_cells <- sum(claims$location == "table_1")
```

Two questions, answered before the detail.

## Does the deposited archive run?

Yes, completely. All five analysis scripts execute without error on a current R installation. There are no `setwd()` calls, no hardcoded absolute paths and no functions called before they are defined, and every package the scripts name still installs from CRAN, `rmeta` and `ggstance` included. Nothing in the deposit needs a substitution to run.

What the archive does not do is write anything. All eight `ggsave()` calls, all three `print.xtable()` calls and the single `sink()` block are commented out in the deposited files, so a clean run leaves nothing behind but a stray `Rplots.pdf` from the plots being printed to a device. There is nothing to diff a rerun against, which is why the maintained rewrite writes its outputs to disk.

## Does the maintained rewrite reproduce the paper?

Mostly, and the exceptions are mostly in the article rather than in the code. Every number the article and its appendix print has been extracted by hand into `ground_truth/published_claims.csv`, `r format(n_published, big.mark = ",")` of them, and `r format(n_published_reproduced, big.mark = ",")` reproduce exactly at the precision the page uses. `r n_published_disagree` disagree and `r n_published_no_counterpart` have no counterpart in the deposit at all.

Most of that total is float cells that a reader would not think of as a table. The four forest plots print an estimate and a standard error beside **every** row, not only beside the pooled summary, which is `r n_figure_cells` published numbers; the 44 per-study appendix figures do the same, which is another `r format(n_appendix_cells, big.mark = ",")`; and Table 1 prints subject and rating counts for each of the 67 studies, which is `r n_table_1_cells` more. All of those reproduce but two.

The disagreements, none of which changes a substantive conclusion:

```{r summary_failures}
claims |>
  filter(match_rewrite == 0) |>
  select(claim_id, value_paper, value_rewrite, defect_locus) |>
  kable(booktabs = TRUE,
        col.names = c("Claim", "Article", "Deposit", "Where the fault lies"),
        caption = "Published numbers the deposit does not reproduce.") |>
  latex_only(\(k) kable_styling(k, latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position"), font_size = 8))
```

```{r locus_counts, include=FALSE}
locus <- claims |> filter(match_rewrite == 0) |> count(defect_locus) |> deframe()
```

`r locus[["paper_internal"]]` are the article contradicting its own data. Five of those are in `errata.qmd`, which renders to `schwarz_coppock_2022_errata.pdf` and sets out `r spelled(n_errata)` numbered items with every correction computed from the deposit at render time; the sixth is the row count of appendix Table A.1, which is a defect in a table rather than in a sentence and is described below. `r locus[["archive"]]` are the deposit disagreeing with the page. The remaining `r locus[["unresolved"]]` are unresolved, in the strict sense that the cause cannot be established from the deposit and guessing at one would be worse than saying so.

**One published figure prints no data at all.** Appendix Figure A.18 is Costa (2020), whose randomized attribute levels are whole tweets. At the width the appendix uses, those row labels push the plotting panel, the points, the intervals, the estimate labels and the axis off the right edge of the page, so the published figure shows a column of truncated sentences, an axis title cut off after four letters, and none of its `r spelled(n_costa)` estimates. The deposited code reproduces the defect exactly, which is why the maintained `figure_a18_costa_1.pdf` looks the same; `figure_a18_costa_1_legible.pdf` is the same `r spelled(n_costa)` estimates redrawn so they can be read, and it is what the errata reprints.

**The significance counts reproduce under no rule.** The article reports that of the 67 estimates, "47 are positive (23 significant) and 18 are negative (11 significant)." The rule the deposited script itself applies, a confidence interval excluding zero, gives `r sig_counts$n_pos_sig_ci` and `r sig_counts$n_neg_sig_ci`. Testing p below 0.05 gives `r sig_counts$n_pos_sig_p05` and `r sig_counts$n_neg_sig_p05`, and cannot be what was done in any case, because `r sig_counts$n_missing_p` of the 67 rows carry no p-value at all. Nor is this a matter of finding the right threshold: both counts rise as a threshold is relaxed, so no threshold produces 23 and 11 together. The threshold that puts 23 estimates in the positive column leaves `r negatives_at_23` in the negative one, and the threshold that reaches 11 in the negative column leaves `r positives_at_11` in the positive one. No corrected value can be stated, so none is; this is recorded as unresolved rather than as an erratum.

Every estimate, standard error, interval and p-value the article reports in prose reproduces exactly. What fails is a set of hand-counted descriptions of those estimates, plus two cells of one appendix figure.

# Paper overview

**Citation**: Schwarz, S. and Coppock, A. (2022). "What Have We Learned about Gender from Candidate Choice Experiments? A Meta-Analysis of Sixty-Seven Factorial Survey Experiments." *The Journal of Politics*, 84(2), 655-668. DOI: 10.1086/716290

**Summary**: Sixty-seven conjoint and factorial candidate choice survey experiments, fielded between 1982 and 2021 in more than twenty countries, all randomized candidate gender alongside other candidate attributes. Each study's treatment effect of being described as a woman is re-estimated on a common footing and the 67 estimates are pooled by random-effects meta-analysis. The pooled effect is a gain of 1.8 percentage points of vote share for women candidates, with a confidence interval from 1.1 to 2.5 points. The effect is larger for white than for Black candidates in the US context (2.2 against 0.9 points), larger among women respondents than men (3.0 against 0.9), and reverses sign among Republicans (-1.4) while running positive among Democrats (4.2) and Independents (3.3).

**What the deposit contains**: five pre-computed summary datasets and five analysis scripts. The individual-level data belong to the authors of the 67 original studies and are not redistributed, so the deposit begins one level up, at estimated ATEs and CATEs with their standard errors. Every number in the article is a function of those five files.

# Original archive reproducibility

```{r repro_table}
tibble(
  Script = c(
    "helpers.R",
    "meta_analyze_sates.R",
    "meta_analyze_cates_cand_race.R",
    "meta_analyze_cates_resp_gender.R",
    "meta_analyze_cates_resp_pid.R",
    "meta_analyze_cates_cand_attributes.R"
  ),
  Status = c(
    "Clean (sourced by all five scripts)",
    "Runs; writes nothing, every output call is commented out",
    "Runs; writes nothing",
    "Runs; writes nothing",
    "Runs; writes nothing. Reports the Independent-Republican p-value from the Democrat-Republican statistic",
    "Runs; writes nothing. Its per-study figure loop is written but its writes are commented out"
  ),
  Resolution = c(
    "No changes required",
    "No changes required",
    "No changes required",
    "No changes required",
    "Corrected in the rewrite; see Errata",
    "Restored in the rewrite as 44 written figures"
  )
) |>
  kable(
    booktabs = TRUE,
    col.names = c("Script", "Status on current R", "Resolution"),
    caption = "The deposited scripts on a current R installation."
  ) |>
  latex_only(\(k) kable_styling(k, latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position", "scale_down"))) |>
  latex_only(\(k) column_spec(k, 2, width = "6cm")) |>
  latex_only(\(k) column_spec(k, 3, width = "4cm"))
```

Nothing here needs fixing to make the archive run. The deprecations are all warnings rather than errors: `geom_errorbarh()` and the `%+%` operator are deprecated in ggplot2 4.0.0 but still work, `reshape2::melt()` and `dcast()` are superseded, and `dplyr::do()` has been superseded since 1.0.0. What is wrong with this archive is the p-value bug documented in the Errata, which is a logic error rather than a run failure.

**`rmeta` and `ggstance` are both still installable.** The maintained rewrite replaces `rmeta::meta.summaries()` with `metafor::rma()` on maintenance grounds rather than availability grounds: `rmeta` has not been updated since March 2018. The two implementations of DerSimonian-Laird agree on every pooled estimate, standard error and interval bound in the paper to more than ten significant figures. `ggstance::position_dodgev()` resolves without incident from ggstance 0.3.7, which `coefplot` pulls in. It is dropped from the rewrite for a different reason: it is inert. Building the layer with and without it puts every point at the same coordinates, because every y value it is asked to dodge is already unique, 954 distinct labels across 954 rows in Figure A.1 and no repeated label within any study in Figures A.2 through A.45.

**What the archive does not produce.** Every write in the deposit is commented out: eight `ggsave()` calls, three `print.xtable()` calls and one `sink()` block. Two of the commented `ggsave()` paths point at a directory that was never part of the deposit (`04_Drafts/current_draft/figures/`). The consequence is that the deposit cannot be checked against itself. There is no committed output to diff a rerun against, and a reader who runs all five scripts sees console output and a `Rplots.pdf` and nothing else. Restoring those writes, so that a rerun can be compared against a committed result, is the single largest change the maintained rewrite makes.

# Errata

This section documents corrections the maintained rewrite makes to the deposited code. Errors in the article itself are a separate document: `errata.qmd`, which renders to `schwarz_coppock_2022_errata.pdf`, sets out the `r spelled(n_errata)` corrections one by one, with each computed from the deposit at render time.

**The Independent-versus-Republican p-value is computed from the wrong statistic.** In `meta_analyze_cates_resp_pid.R`, the block that tests the two differences between pooled partisan CATEs computes the second p-value from the first test's statistic:

``` r
# Archive:
I_R_statistic = I_R_estimate / I_R_std.error,
I_R_p.value = 2 * pnorm(abs(D_R_statistic), lower.tail = FALSE)

# Rewrite:
I_R_p.value = 2 * pnorm(abs(I_R_statistic), lower.tail = FALSE)
```

`I_R_statistic` is computed on the line above and then never used, so the reported Independent-Republican p-value is numerically identical to the Democrat-Republican one.

| Quantity | Published | Original archive | Maintained rewrite |
|---|---|---|---|
| Independent minus Republican, p | not reported | 2.21e-10 (equals the D-R p-value) | 1.06e-07 |

The article states only that "the Republican estimate is statistically significantly different from the Democratic and Independent estimates," which is true of both the wrong value and the right one. No published number changes.

**Not corrected: the trimming rule.** Table 2's last-but-one row is labelled "Trimmed (middle 90% of estimates)" and the text says the row drops "the bottom and top 5% of point estimates." The code keeps estimates above the 2nd percentile and below the 95th, which drops the bottom 3.0 per cent and the top 6.0 per cent and retains 61 of 67 studies, or 91 per cent rather than 90. Correcting 0.02 to 0.05 would be a plausible reading of a typo, but it is a change to a sample definition rather than to a mechanical error, so the rewrite reproduces the published row as computed and reports the alternative separately in `output/table_2_trim_sensitivity.csv`. The symmetric rule the text describes gives 0.020 over 59 studies against the published 0.018 over 61, so the robustness claim the row is making survives either reading.

**Not corrected: the year threshold.** The subset labelled "Post-2014 studies" is selected by `year > 2010`. The labels are nonetheless accurate, because the sample contains no study fielded between 1998 and 2014, a gap the article notes in its fourth footnote, so every threshold in that window produces the same two groups of 63 and 4.

# Ground truth

```{r gt_summary}
gt |>
  count(table_figure, match) |>
  mutate(match = case_when(match == 1 ~ "Reproduces",
                           match == 0 ~ "Does not reproduce",
                           TRUE ~ "Not stated in the article")) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = match, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  rename(`Table or figure` = table_figure) |>
  kable(booktabs = TRUE,
        caption = paste0("Ground truth: ", n_claims,
                         " recorded quantities, by where the article states them.")) |>
  latex_only(\(k) kable_styling(k, latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position")))
```

`ground_truth/schwarz_coppock_2022_ground_truth.csv` records `r n_claims` quantities and answers a question about the deposited code: `value_script` is what the deposited scripts produce through `rmeta`, `value_rewrite` is what `maintained/` produces through `metafor`, and `value_paper` is filled only by reading the article. Where the article does not state a quantity the cell is empty and `match` is `NA`, which is the case for every confidence interval bound in the four figures: the forest plots draw the intervals but label only the estimate and its standard error.

The article's own side of the comparison is exhaustive and lives separately, in the next section.

```{r gt_failures}
gt |>
  filter(match == 0) |>
  select(table_figure, claim, value_paper, value_script, notes) |>
  kable(booktabs = TRUE, digits = 3,
        col.names = c("Table or figure", "Claim", "Article", "Deposit", "Note"),
        caption = paste0("The ", n_fail,
                         " recorded quantities that do not reproduce.")) |>
  latex_only(\(k) kable_styling(k, latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position", "scale_down"))) |>
  latex_only(\(k) column_spec(k, 5, width = "6cm"))
```

# Every published number

The ground truth above was built around the article's floats. That misses the numbers a reader is most likely to quote, which sit in sentences, and it misses the numbers a figure prints on its own face. So the article and its appendix were read end to end and every numeric token extracted by hand into `ground_truth/published_claims.csv`: `r format(n_published, big.mark = ",")` of them, each classified by what would verify it.

```{r claims_types}
claims |>
  count(claim_type) |>
  mutate(claim_type = recode(claim_type,
    pipeline = "Pipeline: the deposit should produce it",
    descriptive = "Descriptive: a claim about shape, sign or a count",
    definitional = "Definitional: a scale point or a design parameter",
    structural = "Structural: a float's own shape",
    transcribed = "Transcribed: copied from another paper")) |>
  arrange(desc(n)) |>
  kable(booktabs = TRUE, col.names = c("What would verify it", "Claims"),
        caption = paste0("The ", format(n_published, big.mark = ","),
                         " numbers the article and appendix print.")) |>
  latex_only(\(k) kable_styling(k, latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position")))
```

Two instruments read those claims against the pipeline, by separate paths from the same outputs. `ground_truth/build_ground_truth.R` writes `ground_truth/published_claims_reproduction.csv`, which puts the pipeline's value beside every published one; `maintained/in_text_claims.R` prints each number beneath the sentence that states it, quoted verbatim. Where one parses the label a plot or a table actually draws, the other formats the estimate behind it. The build runs the claims file, counts what it prints against the extraction, and stops if the two instruments disagree anywhere, so neither can quietly stop checking.

```{r claims_coverage}
claims |>
  mutate(location = if_else(str_detect(location, "^figure_a([2-9]|[1-4][0-9])$"),
                            "figure_a2 to figure_a45", location)) |>
  summarize(Claims = n(),
            Reproduces = sum(match_rewrite == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
            `Does not` = sum(match_rewrite == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
            `No counterpart` = sum(is.na(match_rewrite)),
            .by = location) |>
  arrange(location) |>
  rename(`Where the article prints it` = location) |>
  kable(booktabs = TRUE,
        caption = "Published numbers against the deposit, by where the article prints them.") |>
  latex_only(\(k) kable_styling(k, latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position")))
```

**Every forest plot in the paper is a published table in disguise.** Each prints an estimate and a standard error, in percentage points to one decimal, beside every study row and not only beside the pooled summary. In the four main figures that is `r n_figure_cells` numbers, and in the 44 per-study appendix figures another `r format(n_appendix_cells, big.mark = ",")`. The four main figures are rasterized in the published PDF, so no text search reaches them; they were read off page renderings. All but two reproduce, and the two are both Sen (2017), USA, SSI 2 in Figure 3, where the page prints 6.0 and 0.5 and the deposited respondent-gender file gives 5.9 and 0.4. The deposited study-level file does carry a revised Sen SSI 2 estimate, which Figure 1 reproduces exactly, so the conditional-effects file is one revision behind the figure the article printed. Every one of the `r format(n_appendix_cells, big.mark = ",")` appendix labels reproduces exactly.

**The deposit has no counterpart for `r n_published_no_counterpart` published numbers**, each named with its reason in `build_ground_truth.R`. Twelve are quoted from other people's papers and cannot drift when this pipeline moves. Two are theoretical reference points, a majority threshold and the midpoint of a vote margin. Three are the appendix B validation of the digital measurement procedure, whose average absolute error and correlation compare digital measurements against estimates computed from Kirkland and Coppock's raw data; the deposit carries neither, so those numbers are not reconstructible from it. What the deposit does record is which studies were measured that way, in a free-text note field: the note marks ten experiments in eight papers where the appendix says nine in seven.

**Two further disagreements the float-shaped ground truth could not see.** The design section says the 67 experiments come from 49 papers, where the deposit assigns 50 distinct bibliography keys to them. And Table 2's trimmed row, labelled "middle 90% of estimates" and described in the text as dropping "the bottom and top 5% of point estimates," in fact drops the bottom 3.0 per cent and the top 6.0 per cent, retaining 61 of 67. Both are recorded as unresolved: the deposit is self-consistent in each case and cannot say which of the two readings was intended.

**Substitutions.**

| Deposited | Maintained | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `rmeta::meta.summaries(method = "random")` | `metafor::rma(method = "DL")` | Same DerSimonian-Laird estimator; `rmeta` last updated 2018 |
| `do(tidy(with(., ...)))` | `group_by() \|> reframe(re_meta(...))` | `do()` superseded in dplyr 1.0.0 |
| `reshape2::melt()` and `dcast()` | `pivot_wider()`, or dropped | The melt-dcast-clean_names round trip existed only to line two pooled rows up side by side |
| `geom_errorbarh(height = 0)` | `geom_linerange()` | Deprecated in ggplot2 4.0.0 |
| `ggstance::position_dodgev()` | dropped | Still available, but inert: every y value it dodges is already unique |
| `ggplot() %+% data` | `ggplot(data)` | Deprecated in ggplot2 4.0.0 |
| commented-out `ggsave()`, `print.xtable()`, `sink()` | `ggsave()` and `write_csv()` to `output/` | So that a rerun can be diffed against a committed result |
| `%>%` | `\|>` | Native pipe |

**The estimator is named at every call site.** `re_meta()` in `helpers.R` takes `method` as a required argument rather than defaulting to `DL`, so no script can pool without saying which estimator it pooled with. `table_2_meta_robustness.R` reports both: the DL columns reproduce the published table, and REML columns sit beside them as an addition rather than a correction. REML moves no estimate by more than 0.001 and widens most intervals slightly, which is what a different heterogeneity estimator on 67 studies should do.

**Coverage the archive states but does not deliver.** The deposit's README says `meta_analyze_cates_cand_attributes.R` produces "Figure A.1, Figures A.2 through A.45, Table A.1." It contains the code for all three, with the writes commented out. The rewrite restores the 44 per-study figures, which take four seconds of the run's six. Table A.1 is a partial exception: the published table pairs each study with a prose description of its randomized attributes ("Race, ballot length"), and the deposit carries only the variable names those descriptions were written from, so `table_a1_study_attributes.csv` lists the variable names and the counts instead. The study coverage is the checkable part, and it is where the 43-against-44 discrepancy shows up.

# Rewrite verification

```{r rewrite_table}
gt |>
  filter(!is.na(match)) |>
  transmute(
    `Table or figure` = table_figure,
    Claim = claim,
    Article = value_paper,
    Deposit = value_script,
    Rewrite = value_rewrite,
    `Deposit matches` = match,
    `Rewrite matches` = match_rewrite
  ) |>
  kable(booktabs = TRUE, digits = 3, longtable = latex_out,
        caption = paste0("Every quantity the article states, against the deposit and the rewrite (",
                         n_verifiable, " rows).")) |>
  latex_only(\(k) kable_styling(k, latex_options = c("striped", "repeat_header"), font_size = 8))
```

The rewrite reproduces the deposit exactly. Across all `r n_claims` recorded quantities the two agree to better than 1e-10 in every case but one, the Independent-Republican p-value corrected in the Errata above. Where the deposit fails to match the article, so does the rewrite, which is the intended behaviour: the failures are in counts the article states, not in anything the code computes.

# R environment

```{r r_env}
session <- sessionInfo()
tibble(
  Package = names(session$otherPkgs),
  Version = map_chr(session$otherPkgs, "Version")
) |>
  arrange(Package) |>
  kable(booktabs = TRUE, caption = "Packages loaded when this report was rendered.") |>
  latex_only(\(k) kable_styling(k, latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position")))
```

Rendered under `r R.version.string` on `r session$running`.
